blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: paradigm — Overall style for organising programs.
procedural — Organises a program around sequences of operations and subroutines.
object-oriented — Encapsulates state and behaviour into objects.
functional — Emphasises functions applied to values and reduced side effects.
declarative — Expresses desired results rather than imperative step sequences.

blocks.title: Procedural
blocks.text: Instructions and procedures operate on arguments or shared data. A function can be reused independently.

blocks.title: Object-oriented
blocks.text: The Account object combines state (Balance) and behaviour (Deposit). With inheritance, a subclass can reuse and specialise a class. A virtual method overridden in a derived class supports polymorphism: the actual object decides which implementation runs.

blocks.title: Functional style
blocks.text: Values are transformed using expressions/functions, often emphasising avoiding mutation of existing input data.
